_about.scenario: One intrusion, start to finish: an SSH password guessing run against a single account, a successful login, bulk reads of finance and HR files, three large uploads to an external host, a PowerShell download-and-run, registry and service persistence, failed then successful lateral movement over SMB, a fixed-interval C2 beacon, and finally the Security event log being cleared. Interleaved with a handful of ordinary user actions that must NOT be reported as attacks.
_about.what_this_covers: Recall and precision against a scenario a competent analyst would agree on, and nothing else. It is one synthetic log of 35 rows with a deliberately unambiguous story — it says nothing about performance on noisy production data, on formats other than CSV, or on attacks not represented here. Small on purpose: every label has to be defensible by reading the log, and a set nobody can check by hand is a set nobody will maintain.
_about.labelling_rule: A finding matches a label if any of the label's `match_any` strings appears in the finding's name or description, case-insensitively. Deliberately generous on wording and strict on substance: the model is being measured on whether it saw the event, not on whether it phrased it the way the labeller did.
_about.mitre_note: `mitre` is the technique the labeller considers correct, taken from the vendored ATT&CK catalogue. It is reported as an accuracy figure, not enforced: several of these events map to more than one defensible technique, and grading a model wrong for choosing the other one would measure agreement with the labeller rather than correctness.

expected_attacks.label: SSH password guessing against jmorris
expected_attacks.why: Eleven consecutive auth_failure rows from 203.0.113.44 for one account, two seconds apart, followed by a success.

expected_attacks.label: Bulk upload of finance and HR files to an external host
expected_attacks.why: 8.4 MB posted to storage.example-cdn.net minutes after reading payroll, forecast and salary files.

expected_attacks.label: Run-key and service persistence for C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe
expected_attacks.why: A Run key and a service both pointing at a binary dropped into Temp minutes earlier.

expected_attacks.label: Encoded PowerShell downloading and running a payload
expected_attacks.why: powershell.exe -enc followed by a payload written to C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe.

expected_attacks.label: SMB admin$ sweep across three hosts
expected_attacks.why: Two access-denied attempts on dc01 and dc02 followed by a successful connection to ws33.

expected_attacks.label: Fixed-interval beacon to 192.0.2.200
expected_attacks.why: Four HTTPS beacons of identical size exactly sixty seconds apart, after a DNS lookup of a dynamic-DNS name.

expected_attacks.label: Windows Security event log cleared
expected_attacks.why: The last action in the log, after everything above.

expected_anomalies.label: jmorris active at 01:00–04:00 from an external address
expected_anomalies.why: Every other user in this log acts from the corporate range during working hours.

expected_anomalies.label: 203.0.113.44 as an external source of authentication
expected_anomalies.why: The only non-RFC1918 source of an authentication attempt.

must_not_report.label: rlee reading onboarding.pdf
must_not_report.why: One ordinary file read from the corporate range in working hours. Reporting it is a false positive, and a report that flags routine activity is a report an analyst stops reading.

must_not_report.label: dsingh logging in and exporting a report
must_not_report.why: A successful web console login and an export, from the corporate range, in working hours.
